evidence: app/src/routes/abilities/[name].ts:1-72 — whole ability page is one self-contained route file, deletable as a unit
app/src/document.ts:17-20 — nav has no Abilities link, so nothing to unlink there
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:318 — Abilities section on the Pokémon page must be edited separately
app/src/lib/components.ts:15 — CardData.hiddenAbility ('ability page only') stays behind as dead code unless pruned
app/src/lib/species-cards.ts:43 — entry passthrough exists only for abilities/[name].ts:32 is_hidden; removing Abilities orphans it
app/public/styles/global.css:208 — .hidden-ability, and global.css:402 .abilities-list, must be hunted down in a 559-line stylesheet
removability.rationale: The route itself deletes cleanly, but the feature leaks into the shared card abstraction (hiddenAbility flag, entry passthrough), the Pokémon page and the global stylesheet, so removal is a handful of scattered edits rather than a directory delete.

evidence: app/src/lib/species-cards.ts:42 — sprite selection for move/ability/type card lists lives in one obvious function
app/src/routes/index.ts:118-135 — home page builds its own CardData (sprite at :125) instead of reusing speciesCards, so card fixes have a second site
app/src/routes/index.ts:21-30 — pageUrl builds q/type/generation/page query server-side; app/src/routes/index.client.ts:8-18 — navigate rebuilds the same params client-side
app/src/routes/index.ts:164 — 'context.props.GET as any' (same cast in all 5 routes) means field renames in the handler break templates with no compiler error
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:13 — unused orMissing import; dead code survives because nothing flags it
changeability.rationale: Most reported symptoms trace to one findable place, but card construction and filter-URL building are each implemented twice (server and home vs shared), and pervasive 'as any' casts remove the safety net that would make the duplication safe to change.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:9-70 — base URL, cache, concurrency pool and /api/v2 prefix are confined to one narrow seam; routes only see api() and idFromUrl()
app/src/lib/format.ts:8-56 — display rules (humanize, dexNumber, englishName, MISSING) are pure and page-agnostic
app/src/routes/*.client.ts — client scripts contain no data fetching; all API access is in server handlers (clean server/client separation)
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:61-89 — template emits data-v/data-n/data-missing attributes consumed by [name].client.ts:25-42: an implicit string contract between server and client
app/src/routes/index.ts:174 — id="filter-q" must stay in sync with index.client.ts:16 by hand
coupling.rationale: Modules meet through narrow, well-documented helpers and the server/client split is crisp; the main tangles are stringly-typed DOM contracts between templates and client scripts and untyped handler-props crossing the handler→template boundary.

evidence: app/src/lib/species-cards.ts:25-46 — speciesCards correctly centralizes the alternate-form/species-mapping rule and is reused by three routes; well matched to the real variation
app/src/lib/components.ts:13-15 — CardData grows page-specific optional flags (types 'home page only', hiddenAbility 'ability page only'): mild flag-parameter creep
app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:46-52 — h1/title computed in document() and recomputed in template (:58); same duplication in abilities, types, pokemon routes
app/src/routes/moves/[name].ts:28 — 'gracile-static' guard, try/catch-404 and notFound branch are copy-pasted across five routes with no shared helper

app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:112-113 vs app/src/routes/index.ts:118 — 'default Pokémon of a species' is resolved via varieties lookup here but via the id convention there, two idioms for one domain rule
abstraction_design.rationale: The lib layer (format, components, speciesCards) is the right shape and stretches to new card lists, but the route layer has no abstraction at all for the repeated resource-page skeleton, so a similar-but-different section is a copy-paste of ~60 lines plus per-route flag creep on CardData.

findings.issue: Every route casts its handler props to 'any' ('context.props.GET as any'), discarding Gracile's inferred handler-props typing; renaming a returned field breaks the template silently.
findings.suggestion: Type the handler GET returns and let Gracile infer context.props.GET (per the framework's annotated examples); drop the casts.

findings.issue: Pokémon-card construction (sprite, dex, types) is implemented twice: once here for the home page and once in lib/species-cards.ts:33-46 for the other three lists, so sprite/ordering fixes must be checked in two places.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared cardFromPokemon(record, extras) helper (or let the home page fetch refs and reuse speciesCards) so sprite/type selection has a single home.

findings.issue: The resource-page skeleton — 'url.hostname === \'gracile-static\'' guard, try/catch→404 block, notFound template branch, and h1 computed separately in document() and template() — is copy-pasted across all five routes.
findings.suggestion: Factor small helpers (e.g. loadResource(url) returning a 404-marked result, and resourceTitle(names, fallback) used by both document and template) so the next resource route is a diff, not a clone.

findings.issue: Client scripts are coupled to server templates by strings: 'table.moves-table', the data-v/data-n/data-missing sort attributes, id="game" and id="filter-q"; renaming any of them in a template silently kills interactivity.
findings.suggestion: Centralize these selectors/attribute names in a tiny shared constants module imported by both the template and the client script (or emit them from one place), and add a comment in the template that the client script depends on them.

findings.issue: Filter query-string construction (q/type/generation/page defaults) is duplicated between pageUrl (server) and navigate (client), so a param rename or default change needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Share one buildFiltersUrl(params) helper imported by both the route and the client script.

findings.issue: Build output (app/dist/) sits committed alongside the sources and can go stale, misleading anyone grepping for behavior.
findings.suggestion: Add app/dist/ to .gitignore and rely on 'npm run build'.

findings.issue: All page styles live in one 559-line global stylesheet organized only by comment banners, so removing/adding a feature means hand-hunting its rules (.hidden-ability at :208, .abilities-list at :402).
findings.suggestion: Split into per-route stylesheets (Gracile supports route-scoped style imports) or at least per-page CSS files imported by each route.

findings.issue: Ability-specific concerns leak into shared abstractions: CardData.hiddenAbility flag and the raw 'entry' passthrough in speciesCards (species-cards.ts:27-28,43) exist only to serve abilities/[name].ts:32.
findings.suggestion: Keep speciesCards purely generic (return CardData) and let the ability route look up is_hidden from the entry list it already has.

findings.issue: Unused import (orMissing) — dead code that a linter would have caught; there is no lint/typecheck gate in the app's scripts.
findings.suggestion: Remove it and add a 'check' script (tsc --noEmit or eslint) to package.json.

findings.issue: API records are typed 'any' throughout the handlers (move, species, pokemon, type), so field typos surface only at runtime; only lib/ has local types.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal local interfaces for the ~10 API shapes actually consumed (as lib/species-cards.ts already does for entries) rather than typing the whole API.

summary: A small, idiomatic Gracile 0.11 codebase with a genuinely good data-access seam (one file owns base URL, caching and fetching) and well-factored display helpers; the four card lists largely share one construction path. Editability is held back by copy-pasted route skeletons (guard/404/title logic ×5), duplicated card construction on the home page, stringly-typed DOM contracts between templates and client scripts, and pervasive 'as any' casts that disable Gracile's handler-props typing. Solid, unremarkable: easy to extend by cloning, harder than necessary to refactor safely.
